title: Travel Log
text:
A quick tour of the routes I actually traveled—each stop is a real repo on my GitHub (github.com/linarettig). No epic novel… just stamps in the passport and postcards from the trail.






Leg
Destination (repo)
What it is (one line)




🐛 Debug camp
Debugging-AI
Learning to read errors, test ideas, and stop guessing.


🔁 Portage route
APIs-Functions-Iteration
Functions + iteration so I don’t copy-paste the same trip 50 times.


🗺️ Ridge trail
Geospatial
Maps + spatial workflows: where “CRS panic” becomes “CRS confidence.”


🧪 Summit science
Nested-Modeling
Nested/modeling patterns for analyses that grow beyond one tidy table.


🌬️ Sky sector
Colorado-Air-Quality-Index
Air-quality indicators + plots that explain what the sky is “saying.”


🦌 Park pass
r_finalproject
National park visitation + air-quality patterns—people, places, atmosphere.








Wrangling: dplyr habits that keep datasets from becoming a swamp

Viz: ggplot2 as my “camera” for evidence, not decoration

Space: sf lessons (CRS is a mood, but you can manage it)

Automation: map()-style thinking from the iteration repo

Storytelling: Quarto + GitHub as proof I didn’t just visit the data—I left breadcrumbs






Debugging-AI: The trail teaches you that the fastest “shortcut” is a reproducible tiny example.

APIs-Functions-Iteration: The moment functions clicked felt like upgrading from a paper map to GPS.

Geospatial: My first “real map” souvenir—worth framing if CRS behaved.

Nested-Modeling: When one model becomes many models… organization becomes survival gear.

Colorado-Air-Quality-Index: Clear plots beat clever plots when someone asks “so what?”

r_finalproject: Connecting visitation + air felt like linking two trails into one vista.






Machine learning mountains (tidymodels)

Shiny archipelago (if I want a true interactive island chain)

R package desert oasis (bundle my favorite helpers)

title: Packing List
text:
The light packing list: the gear I actually carry after this semester, plus where I “proved it” on GitHub.





data %>% 
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(date)) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(month = lubridate::month(date)) %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(site) %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(mean_pm25 = mean(pm25, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")



ggplot2::ggplot(data, ggplot2::aes(x, y, colour = group)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ season) +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Plain-language title", x = "X (units)", y = "Y (units)") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()



purrr::map_dfr(paths, readr::read_csv, show_col_types = FALSE)






R for Data Science (2e)

ggplot2 reference

Posit cheatsheets

#rstats + searching with words like tidyverse, sf, reprex








Import → inspect (glimpse, summary)

Fix types + names

Document missingness

Filter → mutate → summarise

Save + commit when it runs





Start with one geom

Add encodings next

Facet if needed

Labels + units + caption

Export the right size (slides vs report)





Plot before you “math”

State the question + null (if testing)

Check assumptions / diagnostics

Write the takeaway in English first








paths <- list.files("data", pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
purrr::map_dfr(paths, readr::read_csv, show_col_types = FALSE)



data |>
  dplyr::group_by(site) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(), mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")



print(my_plot) # sometimes needed depending on context






object not found: spelling + ls() + “did I run the chunk above?”

Join exploded rows: check duplicate keys with count(id, sort = TRUE)

Forgotten package: library() / install once, then restart if needed






tidymodels ridge hike

Shiny archipelago (interactive apps)

Time series trail (tsibble)

Text-mining dunes (tidytext)

Quarto “expedition publishing” upgrades











TipLessons that survived contact with reality




Small rep first — if it doesn’t work tiny, it won’t work huge.

Commit when it runs — future you sends thanks.

Plot early — your eyes are a model too.

Read the error from the top — it’s usually honest.

Celebrate working chunks — progress is cumulative.

title: R Adventures
text:
Name: Lina Rettig Citizenship: Colorado State University
Occupation: Aspiring Data Explorer
Issued: Spring 2026 Valid Through: Forever learning!
Visa Stamps Collected: - ✅ Data Wrangling (dplyr territory) - ✅ Visualization Arts (ggplot2 province) - ✅ Statistical Modeling (Linear Regression region) - ✅ Spatial Analysis (sf kingdom) - ✅ Interactive Dashboards (Shiny islands)



I started this adventure in ESS 523 thinking R was just another programming language. Turns out, it’s a whole world to explore! From the treacherous forests of debugging to the peaks of publication-ready plots, here’s my travel diary.






NoteWhy I Travel in Data



I started learning R after I started my masters in Environmental Engineering with a focus on Indoor Air Quality.






Countries Visited: 12 of topics/projects
Miles Coded: ~6,000 lines of code
Errors Survived: Too many to count 😅
Coffee Consumed: Confidential
Aha Moments: Infinite breakthroughs




Essential Packages: - tidyverse - My Swiss Army knife - ggplot2 - My camera for capturing data beauty - sf - GPS for spatial adventures - rstatix - Medical kit for statistical emergencies - plotly - Interactive tour guide
